They behave like local contractors and they themselves call themselve as a contractor.

1) They’re top management are fraudsters, they will not receive your call or solve any of your issue once your payment is clear.

Local roadside contractor will be more honest, reliable, educated (in terms of architecture) and will deliver your work more efficiently and quickly than this people.

featured_reviews.name: JP Shetty
featured_reviews.review_text:
We had a mixed experience working with this firm. While the design team led by Mrs. Madane is highly talented and creative, the execution managed by Mr. Madane’s side of the business was unacceptably poor.

The Issues:

Failed Supervision: Despite the initial sales pitch, there was zero professional oversight. Project execution was left entirely to contractors with poor workmanship and no understanding of architectural basics.

Major Layout Errors: Most critically, the project was executed using an outdated design layout rather than the finalized one. This resulted in the entire office being shifted 9 inches off-center, misaligned cable ducting, and a "damage control" phase that left us with uneven floor surfaces and cascading structural issues.

Poor Technical Planning: The electrical design was illogical—for example, wiring 18 modular LED lights to a single switch.

Fit and Finish: Five months after handover, we have documented over 100 pending issues. The quality of work is simply not there.

Recommendation: Hire them for Design Only. Do not let them manage the build; find a competent independent contractor for execution.

owner_posts.post_text: Bold yet understated, SJK Architects’ design for the flagship store of Forest of Chintz in Mumbai brings alive India’s glorious, ancient stepwells. The restrained material and colour palette inspires an almost cavernous retail experience – providing a suitable backdrop for the label’s exuberant collections and facilitating an intimate rendezvous with the visitors.

The Resort Hotel in Bodh Gaya uses the power of memory and emotion to create immersive architecture that embodies the tenets of Buddhism. The 78-key hotel Spread over 5-acres responds to the religious tourism in the region - designed as an ode to the historical roots of Buddhism in India.
